title: Title & Registration Services Returned Packets: Start of a Temporary Tag Lapse
content:
When a returned Title & Registration Services packet goes back to the state, the tag lapse starts on the current tag's expiration date recorded on the order when every extension tag that the lower of the service's limit and the registration state's maximum extensions allows has been used and that tag has expired; it starts on the date of the order's most recent return when an extension is still allowed and the current tag has expired; otherwise there is no lapse and it starts on the day the packet goes back.

## Terms on the records

- **Extension tags used**: the temporary tags issued on the title order other than the original tag (the original being sequence 1).
- **Extension limit**: the lower of Kestrel's own extension limit for the service type and the registration state's maximum extensions below.
- **Expired**: the expiration date recorded on the order for the current tag is before the day the packet goes back.
- **Most recent return**: the latest-dated state rejection entry on the title order.

| Registration state | AZ | TX | GA | FL | NC | OH | PA | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| State maximum extensions | 1 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 |

## Decision table

| Extension tags used, compared with the extension limit | Current tag expired | Tag lapse starts on |
|---|---|---|
| equal to or above the limit | yes | the current tag's expiration date recorded on the order |
| below the limit | yes | the date of the order's most recent return |
| any | no | the day the packet goes back (no lapse) |

## Hypothetical illustrations (packet going back on 30 June)

- AZ order, service limit 1, one extension used, current tag expired 12 June: the lapse starts 12 June.
- GA order, service limit 2, one extension used, current tag expired 12 June, most recent return 5 June: the lapse starts 5 June.
- Current tag expiring 3 July: no lapse.
